query: (Cathay MD) Build a model to organise/optimise routes and service so Overall Rating > 7.

per_column.name: cabin_crew_warmth
per_column.rationale: A strong service-quality axis for optimizing toward Overall Rating > 7, going beyond the numeric Staff Service score by adding qualitative texture. Groundedness is good for review-rich rows (e.g. 'best' -> warm, 'no staff to help' -> absent), but the first two samples label warmth as 'robotic_or_absent' when the texts describe ground/gate handling rather than cabin crew, an over-confident read where cabin warmth is not actually stated.

per_column.name: cabin_service_frequency
per_column.rationale: A distinct operational axis (proactivity of in-flight service) useful for service optimization. However several samples assert a frequency category with no textual basis: the Manchester diversion and the Tokyo delay reviews say nothing about in-flight service cadence yet receive 'infrequent_or_absent_between_meals', an unwarranted specific where the source is silent.

per_column.name: food_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: Useful qualitative complement to the Food & Beverages numeric column for driving rating improvement. Well grounded: silent rows correctly return Unknown, and stated cases map sensibly ('food good' -> acceptable/excellent). Minor imprecision (sample 4 'great food options' -> acceptable rather than excellent) but no invention.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizing the specific comfort failure mode (cramped, legroom, malfunction) gives actionable leverage beyond the raw Seat Comfort score. Grounded: silent rows are Unknown, 'seats are cramped... leg space' -> insufficient_legroom is a sound reading. Some rows defaulted to 'adequate' with thin evidence but not contradictory.

per_column.name: cabin_class_value_gap
per_column.rationale: Gap-to-class-expectation is a genuinely useful modeling axis and somewhat distinct from Value For Money. But it forces a value on every row with no Unknown option, producing unsupported reads: the Tokyo delay review (no class/value content) gets 'slight_shortfall' and the diversion review gets 'significant_shortfall', confident specifics the text does not warrant.

per_column.name: special_needs_handling
per_column.rationale: Near-constant boolean (733 false vs 11 true) offering little grouping/modeling leverage for this query. It is well grounded, however: false for rows with no special-needs mention is correct default behaviour, so groundedness stays high while usefulness is limited by the extreme skew.

per_column.name: service_consistency_vs_pre_covid
per_column.rationale: A trend axis (decline vs maintained) could inform where service regressed, offering real analytical angle. Groundedness is mixed: 'first flight after 10 years' -> maintained_or_improved and 'first time no comparison' cases are reasonable, but the diversion row is labelled 'significant_decline' with no pre-covid comparison in the text, an inferred value the source does not support.

judge.rationale: Most columns supply genuinely useful qualitative axes for a service/route optimization model targeting Overall Rating > 7, complementing rather than merely restating the existing numeric ratings; special_needs_handling is the weak link due to its near-constant distribution. Groundedness is generally sound where reviews are rich and silent rows correctly return Unknown/NULL, but several columns (cabin_service_frequency, cabin_class_value_gap, service_consistency_vs_pre_covid) force confident categories onto rows whose text is silent on that dimension, producing observable over-confident inferences that lower overall groundedness.
